title: Dualizing objects compose along a closed immersion in the bounded-below etale comparison class
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell
e\operatorname{char}k$, and $A=A_{E,n}$ for a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ and $n\ge1$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber, def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}S$ be separated finite-type morphisms between separated finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion]. Use the ordinary constant-$A$ module categories on the small etale sites [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For $h=f,g,gf$, let $Rh_!$ be the compactification-independent etale compact-support functor [def-amb-etale-compact-support], and let $h^	imes$ be its ambient right adjoint. These adjoints preserve bounded-below complexes. The mate of the canonical bounded-below composition $Rg_!Rf_!\cong R(gf)_!$ is a natural isomorphism
$$ (gf)^	imes|_{D^+}\xrightarrow{\sim}f^	imes g^	imes|_{D^+}. $$
It identifies the composite counit with the pasted counits. For a closed immersion $i:Z\hookrightarrow T$ between separated finite-type $k$-schemes, let $a_W:W	o\operatorname{Spec}k$ be the structure maps for $W=T,Z$, so $a_Z=a_Ti$. Put $\omega_{W,e}=a_W^	imes A$. Its value at $A$ is the canonical counit-compatible identification $i^	imes\omega_{T,e}\cong\omega_{Z,e}$. Write $
u_W:W_{\mathrm{proet}}	o W_{\mathrm{et}}$ for the site-comparison morphism. Under $Rh_p^!=
u_X^*h^	imes R
u_{Y,*}$ [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] and the site-comparison unit, the same identification on etale-origin bounded-below objects gives $Ri_p^!\omega_{T,p}\cong\omega_{Z,p}$, where $\omega_{W,p}=Ra_{W,p}^!A$.
